commit.message:
Move thread history projection into one blocking task (#49693)

## What changed

Run rollout file opening, metadata lookup, seeking, reading, and record
projection together in a single `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` call. Use
synchronous file I/O in `read_projection_steps_sync` and carry the current
tracing span into the blocking task.

GitOrigin-RevId: a231a8b9a328f6d2e2095a29cde1718ccb6b3901

Keep compressed rollout snippet searches on one blocking worker (#49692)

## Why

Compressed snippet searches schedule a blocking task for every line read. Keeping the scan on one worker avoids repeated task scheduling.

## What changed

Use `RolloutLineReader::find_map` to scan compressed rollouts on a single blocking worker, stopping at the first matching snippet. Preserve read metrics and stop delivering records when the search is canceled, including cancellation during a read.

## Testing

Add tests for first-match snippets, case-insensitive literal matching, malformed records, missing matches, stream errors before a match, and cancellation between lines or during a read.

GitOrigin-RevId: 295206b1a00e861bc44606bd843f6ed8c3e6aae1

Preserve PowerShell relative paths in the elevated Windows sandbox (#49690)

## Why

An inaccessible user profile directory can prevent sandboxed PowerShell from preserving its working directory and resolving relative paths in a project beneath that profile.

## What changed

Pass `USERPROFILE` to elevated setup and refresh. When the command's working directory is beneath an absolute profile path, grant the sandbox group non-inheriting `FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES` access to the profile directory.

Preserve existing permissions and deny ACEs during non-inheriting ACL updates without propagating changes to descendants. Expand generic deny masks when checking for conflicting permissions.

## Testing

Add a Windows regression test that checks PowerShell's working directory and reading `.\public.txt` beneath a protected profile. Add an ACL test that verifies a non-inheriting grant leaves an unprotected child's security descriptor unchanged.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7f142a7ffdee795c3255d4a6e79568fa9391c055

Export skill invocation events through OpenTelemetry (#49689)

## What changed

Emit `codex.skill_invocation` logs for explicit skill injection and detected implicit use, including skill-tool reads. Include skill name, invocation type, conversation, turn, model, and client metadata, plus scope, plugin ID, and ChatGPT user and account IDs when available.

Exclude skill contents, resource paths, email addresses, prompts, and tool payloads. Use the existing OTEL log exporter without an additional opt-in; `otel.exporter = "none"` continues to export no logs.

Document the event fields, exporter configuration, and detection semantics in `codex-rs/otel/README.md`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0f9c492c3f224455f3de3660be89692d776c1951

Deliver remote message board notifications to active turns (#49686)

## What changed

- Start a turn-owned notification receiver using the same remote board client and session identity as the board tools. Deliver post previews as agent messages and cancel the receiver when the turn stops, aborts, or errors.
- Wait for the initial connection attempt before inference, then retry failed or disconnected streams without waking idle agents.
- Skip malformed notices, mismatched recipients or turns, and oversized previews. Reject delivery to stale or canceled turns and bound remote notices to a 1 KiB context budget.

## Testing

Extend remote board tests to cover interrupted setup, connection failures, reconnection, invalid and stale notices, preview delivery into model context, and receiver shutdown after turn completion.

GitOrigin-RevId: c7c8d977fe74b7a5cb3bd8216dc0146f3f297e44

Add a managed feature gate for in-app voice (#49683)

## What changed

Register `in_app_voice` as a stable, default-enabled feature and add it to the configuration schema. The gate is intended for managed requirements to control permission for voice in desktop apps; permission does not establish voice availability or provider support.

## Testing

Add app-server coverage for reporting `in_app_voice = false` from `requirements.toml` in both requirements and feature-list responses. Extend the CLI feature-list test to verify that cloud-managed requirements disable the gate despite a user-configured `true` value, without rewriting the user configuration.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6ec3bc0176fdb3e1714b0136bf812bd56591f6a1

Escape command drafts when recovering question answers (#49678)

## Why

When a turn ends, recovered question answers are appended to the composer draft. If that draft starts with a shell or slash command, submitting the combined text can interpret it as a command instead of a prompt.

## What changed

Escape command prefixes before appending recovered answers so the combined draft stays editable and submits as literal prompt text. Convert shell mode's separate `!` prefix into escaped composer text, and leave slash-prefixed paths such as `/tmp/file` unchanged.

Keep prefix escaping and answer recovery in the same Vim undo edit.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for immediate and queued submission, whitespace around command prefixes, slash-prefixed paths, and already escaped commands. Extend Vim undo coverage to shell and slash command drafts, including shell mode, and add a snapshot of the recovered shell draft.

GitOrigin-RevId: 03c40f72a834a65bf367103cb9170a86dc35ad98

Serialize Responses routing fields before large inputs (#49675)

## Why

Gateways that inspect request bodies incrementally need routing fields before potentially multi-megabyte prompts so they can route requests without buffering the input first.

## What changed

Serialize `model`, `stream`, and optional `service_tier` before `input` in both HTTP Responses requests and WebSocket `response.create` messages. Preserve field values and omission of unset `service_tier`.

## Testing

Add an HTTP regression test with a 2 MiB input that checks routing field order and unchanged JSON contents. Extend WebSocket serialization coverage to assert the routing fields appear first, and check that HTTP requests omit unset `service_tier`.

GitOrigin-RevId: dbc174e1fe7ca30d0c00f075bc37dd5f97b27b37

Allow managed requirements to disable the Windows MXC sandbox (#49642)

## Why

`windows.allowed_sandbox_implementations` permits MXC regardless of the listed implementations. Managed requirements need a separate way to block both explicit MXC configuration and automatic selection through `prefer_mxc`.

## What changed

Add the optional managed requirement `windows.allow_mxc`. Setting it to `false` disables automatic MXC selection and rejects explicit `windows.sandbox = "mxc"` configuration with an error identifying the requirement. Leaving it unset or setting it to `true` preserves existing behavior.

## Testing

Add coverage for the requirement alongside allowed sandbox implementations, preference resolution, and cloud-managed opt-out behavior for implicit, elevated, and explicit MXC configurations.

GitOrigin-RevId: a458a7b4c92cf17e687dbbad8208884d1c097da5

Use server authentication for explicit remote session commands (#49624)

## Why

Session commands with `--remote` should use the selected server's authentication and execution environment, even when the caller has workload identity configured and cannot read its identity token.

## What changed

Connect `queue`, `archive`, `unarchive`, and `delete` directly to the explicit remote app server after validating configuration. Skip caller credential and runtime initialization, use remote thread parameters, and preserve the caller's working-directory override.

## Testing

Add end-to-end coverage with an unreadable caller identity token to verify queued turns use the server's API key and remote archive, unarchive, and deletion operate on the selected server. Add configuration-validation coverage for all four commands and `--no-daemon` rejection coverage for remote unarchive and delete.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5da7abbb40506cd754a8863e1a9d8fad9b1f09a9

Reuse unchanged history snapshots when resuming threads (#49600)

## Why

Resuming a thread rereads persisted history even when a preloaded snapshot is unchanged. Reusing that snapshot must still account for writes committed before writer ownership is acquired.

## What changed

- Carry optional, non-serialized revisions from stored history and model context through thread and agent resume paths.
- Validate the revision under writer ownership and reuse the shared snapshot when it matches. Reload stored history when the revision is missing or changed, while preserving explicit history overrides.
- Resolve the selected rollout before loading context, validate compressed snapshots before materialization, and enforce archived-thread restrictions on canonical paths.

## Testing

Extend coverage for snapshot reuse and late-write refresh in legacy and paginated histories, compressed rollout reuse, archived rollout symlinks, and cold child restoration that includes edits made after preloading history.

GitOrigin-RevId: e1fd7aee6ef2b30f41951e6b7e6b01c3e1420cab

Return authoritative replay history when resuming a thread (#49599)

## Why

A stored history snapshot can become stale before a resumed thread acquires writer ownership. Resume must include writes committed before that acquisition.

## What changed

Make `ThreadStore::resume_thread` return the replay context and use it for session restoration and metadata initialization. The local store refreshes stored snapshots while holding writer ownership, reads through the installed writer to honor explicit rollout paths, and releases the writer if loading context fails. Explicit histories without a canonical session header retain their override semantics.

## Testing

Extend resume tests to cover edits made after the initial snapshot in both legacy and paginated history modes, stale SQLite rollout paths, and preservation of explicitly supplied history.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2361f524d324c859f5dfcf2863320e2045736c2e

Persist explicit user goal edits in model history (#49598)

## Why

User goal edits and clears need to reach the model as user instructions, including when a thread is unloaded or history is being compacted. Automatic goal lifecycle updates must not supply user authorization.

## What changed

- Add optional `origin` values of `user` and `automatic` to `thread/goal/set` and `thread/goal/clear`, and mark TUI goal requests as user actions. Omitted origins do not supply user authorization.
- Persist explicit user objective, status, and clear instructions before changing goal state. Recording failures leave goal state unchanged.
- Coordinate goal edits with thread resume, reload stored history under writer ownership, and preserve edits accepted after the compaction input snapshot.
- Update generated protocol schemas and TypeScript and Python bindings.

## Testing

Add coverage for user edits and clears on loaded and unloaded threads, concurrent path-based resume, exclusion of automatic goals from user instructions, preservation of edits during compaction, and recording failures that leave goal state unchanged.

GitOrigin-RevId: d779d7c678a0c32a6ef76975dbe5b1400d1df245

Make the strict network approval test independent of request order (#49595)

## Why

Guardian and parent requests can arrive in either order after a command yields. A shared response sequence can let parent requests consume Guardian review decisions.

## What changed

Match Guardian responses separately and drive parent responses from the latest tool output in the strict automatic network review test. Poll running sessions with `write_stdin` until the process exits, and assert that the command and network request each receive Guardian review.

GitOrigin-RevId: 21300abd65a3b2d439e8c1ea04e4429d5bd528dd

Skip host skill discovery for Guardian reviews (#49584)

## Why

Guardian does not consume skills, but host skill discovery can block its startup or turn creation when the primary executor is offline.

## What changed

Skip plugin and skill warmup during Guardian session initialization, and use an empty host skills snapshot when building Guardian turn contexts.

## Testing

Add a regression test that discovers skills for the parent session, disconnects its primary executor, and verifies that Guardian still reviews and denies a network permission request.

GitOrigin-RevId: 3c12129721c82cb78a3fa618d6b05faea631966a

Copy selected file paths as plain text in the TUI (#49564)

## Why

Copying a rendered local file target such as `repo/foo_bar!` should preserve the selected path without adding Markdown escapes.

## What changed

Treat selections contained within rendered file targets as plain text, including partial selections and targets in tables. Coalesce adjacent file targets and inline code into literal ranges while preserving Markdown escaping when the selection includes surrounding content.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for partial paths, adjacent literal spans, styled links, table cells, special characters, and mixed selections at narrow and wide rendering widths.

GitOrigin-RevId: 94bcdacf14b013f9198cb84adfdb237eb644dd48

Add an opt-in model catalog to multi-agent context (#49560)

## Why

Refreshing available model descriptions changes the `spawn_agent` tool schema. Keep model choices current while preserving tool definitions and earlier conversation input.

## What changed

- Add the disabled-by-default `model_catalog_in_context` feature for multi-agent V1 and V2. When enabled and model overrides are available, move model listings from tool descriptions into developer `<model_catalog>` messages.
- Include picker-visible, compatible models with descriptions, reasoning efforts, and service tiers in a listing bounded to 1,000 bytes. Point `spawn_agent` guidance to the latest catalog.
- Append updated listings only when their rendered content changes, restore missing listings, and invalidate retained catalogs when they no longer apply.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for V1 and V2 with the feature enabled and disabled. Verify that catalog refreshes preserve tool definitions and prior input when enabled, append the updated listing once, and retain the existing tool-description behavior when disabled. Add a request-history snapshot for the V1 opt-in path.

GitOrigin-RevId: 67b11b4ad6c35f00d0e29edf6343bb0b4804d797

Add a fork shortcut to the TUI command center (#49517)

## What changed

- Fork the selected conversation and open the new session with `f`, configurable through `agents.fork` in the TUI keymap.
- Move the default search shortcuts to `F3` and `/`, preserving unshadowed defaults when custom bindings conflict.
- Keep queued input on the source conversation while attaching and forking, and require closing an open side conversation before forking another task.
- Expose the fork action in command-center help and the keymap picker.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for queued-input preservation, side-conversation protection, configurable fork shortcuts, metadata editing, disconnected actions, and search fallback bindings. Update help and keymap snapshots.

GitOrigin-RevId: b11ae21ef6a2053609b31ce97c646104f18806a3

Add regression coverage for account switches between analytics batches (#49489)

## What changed

Add a debug-only analytics test that switches accounts after the first isolated event request. Assert that only the first request reaches the server and carries the original account's credentials, so subsequent batches do not send stale credentials after the switch.

Remove an unused `ToolCallSource` import.

GitOrigin-RevId: e66904c7a7176f1eaa37662b836132586328884a

Add experimental thread prediction protocol types (#49480)

## What changed

Define `thread/prediction/request` with `threadId` and `sourceTurnId`, and `thread/prediction/updated` with a `completed` result containing optional text or a `failed` result.

Update generated JSON schemas, TypeScript types, and Python notification models. Route prediction notifications to their thread in the TUI and ignore them in the chat widget.

The request remains unimplemented and returns a method-not-found error.

GitOrigin-RevId: 09922f583d5c56f808d018121c651dcd92734515

Discover and validate MCP authorization servers before ID-JAG exchange (#49478)

## What changed

Add `exchange_ema_auth_token` to discover and validate the MCP resource's authorization server before resolving enterprise identity credentials and performing the ID-JAG token exchange. Keep the lower-level exchange primitive private.

- Probe `server/discover` with the enterprise-managed authorization extension, support recognized legacy discovery rejections, and follow protected-resource metadata challenges or well-known fallbacks.
- Match configured resource and issuer constraints, require advertised public-client JWT bearer support, and validate token endpoint metadata without requiring an authorization endpoint.
- Bound discovery with a shared timeout, redirect and authorization-server limits, reject cross-origin metadata redirects, and restrict private authorization-server destinations while allowing local loopback discovery.

## Testing

Add tests covering resource and issuer mismatches before identity access, metadata capability validation, query preservation, modern challenges, JSON and SSE legacy fallback behavior, cross-origin redirect rejection, and private or malformed issuer destinations.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9a55233a20ff42c293f9bd8175e01141ac2d8576

Complete turn abort callbacks before emitting terminal events (#49475)

## Why

`TurnAborted` could be emitted before extension abort callbacks finished, allowing consumers to observe a terminal event while lifecycle cleanup was still pending.

## What changed

Await `on_turn_abort` within task abort handling before emitting `TurnAborted`, retaining callback delivery for already-cancelled tasks. Document that `on_turn_stop` and `on_turn_abort` complete before their corresponding terminal events, if emitted.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for interrupt, conditional interrupt, and shutdown. Hold the abort callback open to verify that `TurnAborted` waits for completion, then verify that the callback runs exactly once with the expected turn ID and abort reason.

GitOrigin-RevId: f34d7e94d04c02544178dc445b85abc65a6ce499

Use the rmcp SDK for enterprise-managed token exchanges (#49473)

## What changed

Upgrade `rmcp` to a pinned Git revision of version `3.3.0` and enable `auth-enterprise-managed`. Delegate the two-stage ID-JAG exchange and token validation to the SDK, replacing the local implementation while retaining Codex HTTP routing and credential lifecycle policy.

Map SDK errors by exchange stage so `invalid_grant` distinguishes enterprise identity failures from resource authorization failures, and preserve handling of `insufficient_user_authentication`.

## Testing

Update exchange tests to verify rejection of unsupported `authorization_details` and malformed signed scopes. Exercise errors from both token endpoints to check credential policy, prevent credential reflection in diagnostics, and ensure rejected grants are not retried.

GitOrigin-RevId: a56034aa3fd70002754ea552fd2da70bdcd85b31

Use server-authoritative permissions in the TUI (#49472)

## Why

Client permission definitions and constraints can differ from those on the connected app server. Accepted permission changes also need to survive task transitions before their settings notifications arrive.

## What changed

- Discover permission profiles and availability from the connected server and apply selections through `thread/settings/update`, including custom profiles.
- Adopt the server's effective permission settings instead of reapplying local definitions or constraints.
- Retain accepted selections and effective approval settings across new tasks, forks, side conversations, directory changes, reconnects, and safety retries without blocking navigation on a settings notification.
- Recognize the current built-in permission preset when the server supplies an unnamed profile.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for conflicting client/server profile definitions, rejected and unchanged selections, consecutive requests with omitted approval settings, and permission carryover before confirmation. Extend discovery and menu tests to verify server-provided availability and unnamed-profile highlighting.

GitOrigin-RevId: bcd767b58dc92dc4f945189078e51e6e5fce6d24

Restore executor tool paths after login shell startup (#49467)

## Why

Login shell startup can reset `PATH`, preventing commands and their children from finding bundled tools such as `rg` in executor-reported directories.

## What changed

When `login_shell_package_path` is enabled, prepend missing executor-reported directories to `PATH` inside the POSIX login shell before running the requested command. Preserve existing entries and the order of newly added directories, and export `PATH` for child commands.

Respect explicit `PATH` overrides and preserve the requested login mode when directories are unusable or `PATH` is read-only. Keep shell diagnostics and `$LINENO` aligned with the original script, including when directory names contain newlines. The feature remains disabled by default.

## Testing

Add shell tests for nested tool lookup, existing entries, quoting, line numbers, and read-only `PATH`. Extend remote execution tests to cover feature gating, explicit overrides, unusable directories, and preservation of the original command in execution events.

GitOrigin-RevId: 301aa34e72cc6292293693250e190c19903f390a

Use `memrchr` to find newlines in reverse JSONL scans (#49444)

Replace the byte-by-byte reverse newline search with `memchr::memrchr` and add `memchr` as a dependency of `codex-rollout`.

GitOrigin-RevId: b07e42e15efb0d63d7b00ee9a2ee29c446f4cf59

Honor server retry advice across Responses retries and fallback (#49441)

## Why

Responses overload and exhausted-request errors could terminate despite server retry advice, and WebSocket-to-HTTP fallback could issue a request before the advised deadline.

## What changed

- Allow `ServerOverloaded` and `RetryLimit` errors to retry when server advice is present, within the configured retry budgets.
- Preserve `Retry-After` headers from rejected WebSocket upgrades and wait for the server deadline before falling back to HTTP.
- Keep quota, usage-limit, and policy failures terminal even when they include retry advice.

## Testing

Add coverage for HTTP overload and rate-limit recovery, WebSocket upgrade rejection and fallback timing, retry deadline preservation through error mapping, and retry limits for sampling and manual and automatic compaction.

GitOrigin-RevId: 72d30a9f078652664754dfa971fd7dc7a78f20e8

Add local audio device selection to TUI voice settings (#49437)

## Why

Voice conversations previously opened the system-default microphone and speaker. Users need to choose which local devices to use, including when connected to a remote app server.

## What changed

- Add input and output device pickers alongside voice selection, with back navigation and a System default option.
- Persist selections as `audio.microphone` and `audio.speaker` on the TUI's machine, excluding project configuration layers. Apply them to the next voice conversation.
- Enumerate devices without opening audio streams and pass the selected names to the voice helper at startup.
- Disable ambiguous device names in the picker and use the same eligibility filtering for discovery and named-device startup.

## Testing

Add tests for device preference persistence across project and remote transitions, picker navigation and duplicate names, discovery without capture, and forwarding selected devices to the helper.

GitOrigin-RevId: d48fb3a09fa9b982a408f5a7c96bdd81776af21d

Preserve bootstrap discovery across authentication changes (#49432)

## Why

Embedded app-server configuration discovery must remain available after login and workspace changes, while content access granted to the previous account must be revoked.

## What changed

Give `AuthRouteConfig` a separate application network policy and bind embedded bootstrap authentication to the effective application policy. Use that policy for account-owned content clients and invalidate it when the authenticated owner changes, preserving the local, endpoint-restricted bootstrap policy.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering bootstrap discovery across login, workspace changes, and sign-out; revocation of previous account clients and permits; and continued enforcement of bootstrap endpoint restrictions and local requirements.

GitOrigin-RevId: 083933e69508224f8232349ba3750c02329af06a

Enable analytics by default for daemon-launched app servers (#49426)

## Why

Daemon-launched app servers should use the same analytics default as first-party clients while honoring explicit user opt-outs.

## What changed

Pass `--analytics-default-enabled` when the PID backend launches an app server, with or without remote control. Users can still disable analytics with `analytics.enabled = false` in `config.toml`.

## Testing

Update argument assertions for both remote-control modes and the daemon start/restart test to expect the analytics flag alongside launch feature overrides.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8a222a00fc56737f5fe2b0385abf59466d1a6671

Prune diagnostic logs periodically by age and database size (#49425)

## Why

Startup-only cleanup leaves expired logs in long-running sessions, and age-based retention alone does not limit database usage.

## What changed

Run cleanup in the background immediately after initialization and every 30 minutes. Start with the existing 10-day retention window, then halve it until occupied SQLite pages fit within a 64 MiB budget or the window reaches one second. Preserve logs within that final second even when they exceed the budget.

Exclude free pages from the budget so SQLite can reuse them, and retain the passive checkpoint after the first sweep. Stop the task when the runtime is dropped or the log pool is closed.

## Testing

Add tests for the 10-day boundary, repeated retention-window halving, free-page accounting, the one-second retention floor, immediate startup cleanup, and periodic cleanup without new writes or a restart. Update existing log tests to use current timestamps so background retention does not remove their fixtures.

GitOrigin-RevId: c6eeb5ec13006d4a03354e08322827429be53ce8

Infer Windows UNC paths with forward and mixed slashes (#49424)

## Why

`LegacyAppPathString` treated `//server/share/project` as POSIX, losing its UNC interpretation when inferring a `PathUri`.

## What changed

Infer Windows syntax whenever an API path starts with two separators, including forward and mixed slashes, independently of the host. For example, `//server/share/project` now converts to `file://server/share/project`. Double-slash POSIX paths require an explicit `PathConvention::Posix`; inferred paths still undergo validation.

## Testing

Add regression tests for UNC and namespace paths, mixed separators, URI serialization round trips, explicit POSIX conversion, convention mismatches, and malformed UNC paths.

GitOrigin-RevId: 720893de517addb7a938e6784d1ed0f05df3ec0d

Omit payloads from multiline ANSI warnings (#49416)

## Why

`ansi_escape_line` logged the rendered contents of every line when given multiline input, allowing large payloads to inflate warning logs.

## What changed

Replace line contents in the warning with structured `input_bytes` and `line_count` fields. Preserve the existing behavior of returning the styled first line.

## Testing

Enable unit tests for `codex-ansi-escape` and add coverage with small and 128 KiB tails, asserting the exact warning fields and preservation of first-line styling.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4be985b4442eaa12f7fdee8a583d6e9714c618d8

Truncate input text in protocol debug output (#49415)

## What changed

Use `derive_more::Debug` for `ContentItem` and `UserInput` to limit debug formatting of `ContentItem::InputText` and `UserInput::Text` to a prefix of at most 512 bytes, ending at a UTF-8 character boundary. Append the full text length in bytes to each preview.

GitOrigin-RevId: ca711dde8f0e3ba7047103415dbc1836f6401e61

Filter graceful shutdown guard and trigger traces from SQLite logs (#49414)

## What changed

Set the default SQLite log filter to `DEBUG` for `tokio_graceful::guard` and `tokio_graceful::trigger`, dropping their `TRACE` events while retaining debug and higher-level diagnostics.

## Testing

Extend the SQLite sink filter test to verify that guard and trigger traces are dropped, their debug events are retained, and `tokio_graceful::shutdown` trace events remain available.

GitOrigin-RevId: c98495c834db35f3d8799ab4f0a1f7a82a53c8ef

Bind the app-server time provider to a local variable (#49411)

GitOrigin-RevId: c0725029a8e58d384d17ff50d99030cc7d1c9e96

Compare tool call metadata in the recorder refresh test (#49408)

## What changed

Update the replay assertion in the recorder refresh test to compare `executed_tool_call_metadata()` instead of entire response items. This keeps the assertion focused on preserving recorded tool call metadata across a configuration refresh.

GitOrigin-RevId: 763173a918f4e0bc79c3c04466453cafb9629775

Recover exec-server sessions after environment info timeouts (#49407)

## Why

A stuck transport can fill the outbound queue, leaving an `environment/info` request blocked while sending. The timeout must cover sending as well as waiting for a response.

## What changed

Wrap the live metadata RPC in a 30-second timeout. On timeout, close the probed connection and request session recovery, returning the timeout error without retrying the failed request. Document the experimental `environment/info` endpoint and its timeout behavior.

## Testing

Extend the WebSocket session recovery test to cover an unanswered `environment/info` request, checking that it times out, closes the connection, and resumes the same session while retaining the client instance.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9035d2edab3626e780d8bd40ebcdf0ca327bfddb

Support explicit cyber access programs with OpenAI API keys (#49406)

## What changed

Forward explicit `cyberAccessProgram` selections for the built-in OpenAI provider when both `api_key_cyber_access_programs` and `api_key_model_discovery` are enabled. The new feature defaults to disabled and can be toggled through the app server's experimental feature enablement API.

Reject explicit selections in OpenAI API-key sessions when either feature is disabled, instead of silently omitting the program. Leave entitlement and model restrictions to the server, and preserve the requested program when a server rejection triggers transport retries.

## Testing

Add app-server coverage for both feature gates, forwarding all three program values, and server rejection without fallback. Update core coverage for API-key resumes with disabled features and custom-provider omission.

GitOrigin-RevId: aa639afb841aa651b28f6f3f61198299372baa2d

Add an experimental flag for bundled tools in login shells (#49403)

## What changed

Register `login_shell_package_path` as a disabled-by-default experimental feature and add it to the configuration schema. Expose it in `/experimental` as “Bundled tools in login shells,” with a description explaining its intended use when login shell startup resets `PATH`.

## Testing

Extend the experimental feature metadata snapshot test to cover the new feature's label, description, and unchecked default state.

GitOrigin-RevId: dc110486ccd8d2d76ac788ba5a413a1374699ff8

Preserve live tool-call metadata across request windows (#49401)

## Why

Persistence and aggregate metadata budgets can omit tool-call observations that are still relevant to the current request, including tool result metadata needed during compaction.

## What changed

- Retain live direct-call observations separately from bounded persisted outputs, keyed by response item ID so reused call IDs cannot mix results.
- Restore those observations for sampling and compaction, pruning them only when sampling confirms they have left the history window. Preserve observations across shortened compaction retries.
- Remove aggregate prompt metadata caps while retaining per-call argument limits and the outgoing message size limit. Invalidate cell completeness when argument normalization truncates a recorded call.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for exhausted persistence budgets, reused call IDs and reversed completion order, shortened compaction retries, and completeness after argument truncation. Extend integration coverage for large Code Mode metadata, provider metadata support, and fork/resume behavior.

GitOrigin-RevId: 004082b69bff9cc8b05f36d1052057f163c67f07

Remove randomized greetings from TUI session headers (#49395)

## What changed

Remove startup greeting phrases and the shared greeting state from startup drafts, session headers, and the empty-state animation. Raw session headers now consistently include `model:` and `directory:` fields.

## Testing

Update startup and fresh-thread snapshots to omit greetings, and adjust raw-header assertions to check model and directory fields.

GitOrigin-RevId: 531b5ba42d7a88f86b1c7f69030f3560abc25198

Add attributed MCP OAuth credential storage telemetry (#49392)

## What changed

- Instrument MCP OAuth loads, saves, deletes, fallback cleanup, and refresh persistence with credential-free storage metrics, distinguishing configured policy from operations on a pinned store.
- Retain the originating client across background tasks, blocking storage operations, and session recovery, including recovery after startup found no credentials.
- Preserve typed keyring and lock error categories for metrics and remove raw error details from storage warnings.

## Testing

Add tests for policy and pinned-store outcomes, best-effort cleanup failures, wrapped lock errors, and successful or failed refresh persistence without duplicate observations. Add recovery tests that verify client attribution after anonymous startup and across threads with different originators.

Treat explicit provider model catalogs as authoritative (#49135)

## Why

Providers with `model_catalog_url` could advertise bundled models absent from their catalog or reuse stale models after a failed refresh. Model metadata could also match by prefix or namespaced suffix instead of the provider's exact model ID.

## What changed

- Suppress bundled model fallback and merging for explicit provider catalogs, including when discovery is disabled.
- Require unique, non-empty catalog slugs and match metadata by exact model ID.
- Serialize explicit catalog refreshes and invalidate in-memory and persisted catalog entries after fetch failures, preventing stale cache reuse.
- Report a clear configuration error when startup has no available model, while allowing an explicitly configured `model`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for exact model matching, hidden catalog entries, cache invalidation across restart and recovery, invalid slugs, and empty-catalog startup with and without an explicit model. Update app-server model-list expectations and verify the TUI configuration error.

Resume unsent TUI input after reconnecting (#49105)

## Why

Reconnecting paused all recovered input, including queued messages that had never been sent. Those messages can resume automatically once any uncertain submissions are resolved.

## What changed

- Track unsent and unconfirmed messages separately. Reconcile submitted prompts and steers using exact client message IDs from restored history, buffered events, and later receipts.
- Remove confirmed submissions from the recovered queue and resume unsent input after replay. Keep uncertain submissions paused without resending them, and show a notice identifying the message whose delivery could not be confirmed.
- Preserve pauses for unavailable conversations, pending compact/review requests, and existing input recovery failures.
- Simplify reconnect status text and remove blanket disconnect/reconnect transcript notices.

## Testing

Update reconnect integration tests and snapshots for automatic queue resumption. Add coverage for matching and unrelated receipts, missing history, late confirmations across navigation, pending compaction, and preservation of image-failure recovery pauses.
